name: Side-Lying Hip Abduction
description: Side-lying hip abduction is performed lying on one side and raising the top leg toward the ceiling with a straight knee, working the hip abductors through a longer lever than the clamshell. The gluteus medius and tensor fasciae latae are the primary movers, and the exercise is a staple of both rehabilitation programs and general glute training. A resistance band above the ankles or a cable at the ankle increases the load.

execution.starting_position: Lie on one side with hips stacked and legs straight. Bottom arm extended under the head. Body in a straight line.
execution.setup_instructions: Use bodyweight or add a mini loop band above the ankles for added resistance.
steps: Step 1: Lie on your side with hips stacked, legs extended, body in a straight line.
Step 2: With the top leg straight and toes pointing slightly downward, raise the leg toward the ceiling by abducting the hip.
Step 3: Raise until 45–60° of abduction or until the pelvis begins to tilt.
Step 4: Hold briefly at the top, then lower under control.
Step 5: Complete all reps on one side then switch.
execution.breathing_instructions: Exhale as you raise the leg. Inhale as you lower.
common_mistakes: Rolling the pelvis forward or back — keep hips stacked vertically
Internally rotating the hip (toes pointing up) — slight external rotation keeps glute medius engaged
Using momentum — the movement should be slow and controlled
safety_considerations: Very low-risk exercise suitable for beginners and rehabilitation
Avoid if the exercise reproduces hip or groin pain
execution.range_of_motion_guidance: Raise the leg to about 45–60°. Stop before the pelvis tilts.
coaching_cues: Raise with the outer hip, not the lower back
